output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification and distinctions (floor block, date), then competing-hypotheses weighing; provenance noted. No extra evidence collected.
output.brief: The August dip is almost entirely a cooling failure, not the contractor or the kiosks. Chiller CH-2, which serves floors 6-8, failed on 4 August and wasn't fixed until 19 August. Rooms ran at 26-29 C. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and their scores dropped only for guests checking out 5-20 August. They recovered to 8.4 after the repair. Floors 1-5 were flat. Cleanliness scores and inspection pass rates didn't move, and kiosk scores, usage and queue times were steady. Neither the survey method nor the contractor explains the dip. The preventive maintenance on both chillers was deferred in April under a budget hold, which likely left the chiller exposed. I'm fairly sure (about 90%) of the cooling cause. The rate rise may have added a little to the value-score dip, but the normal August dip hides it. My recommendations: do not serve notice on Orrin, and do not pull the kiosks. Reinstate the chiller maintenance, keep critical spares on site, and write a cooling-outage guest-recovery protocol. Don't exclude the floor 6-8 responses, because that would hide a real failure and flatter a bonus-linked score. Don't reverse the rate rise yet. Watch the value score over the next few months. A return-stay offer to affected guests is optional, since they already received an apology and a credit.
